applicabilityBasis.summary: Official documents describe MONEY as a transferable, USD-denominated permissionless CDP stablecoin minted by depositing BTC or ETH collateral and opening loans. Automated Loan Protection trades collateral within price bands. These materials do not identify a legal issuer obligated to redeem holders for national currency or a national-currency bank deposit. The May 7, 2025 sunset notice ends team and interface support while preserving smart-contract access. Historical general stablecoin use and the unresolved statutory issuer obligation support unclear applicability rather than a categorical non-payment-token exemption.

genius.notes: Reviewed 2026-10-07. The official sunset notice schedules interface shutdown for June 1, 2025 and ends core development and support effective May 7, 2025; contracts remain available for direct position management. No legal token issuer, domicile or fixed monetary-value redemption obligor is assigned. Collateral-mechanics documentation is not evidence of a current reserve disclosure or reserve attestation, so reserveDisclosurePresent, reserveDisclosureUrl and monthlyAttestationPresent are omitted. No public GENIUS authorization or token-specific issuer intent was found in the consulted sources. No enforcement status is assigned from a bounded authorization search. Unknown pathway and foreign-exception fields do not assert authorization or rejection. DASP posture refers to the GENIUS statutory timetable, not unconditional permission under other laws.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, the reopened OCC pending digital-asset bank-charter table, OCC proposal, Federal Register SCRC procedure, Federal Reserve proposal, NYDFS directory and token documents, together with token/entity-specific official-domain searches, did not identify a qualifying public GENIUS issuer approval, state qualification, pending GENIUS application or registered foreign exception for this token. The OCC table is not an exhaustive GENIUS issuer register; general rulemaking and ordinary licenses are not token-specific authorization. This bounded public-evidence finding does not exclude confidential or unpublished filings.
